scenarios.title: Vault: Sell removes the records at once and credits the engine's price to the stash gold
scenarios.provenance: SETUP (CHEATED, mechanics only): level, gold and stash gold by stat verbs; the six unidentified vault records are real magic items given by `debug give ... unid` and taken into the vault by the runner. UNMEASURED run: the sale credits the stash with `debug creditgold` (ADR 0029 amendment, player-ordered write, refused under --lockstep), so the bot phase runs d2d in real time with --vault-pay; the one creditgold write per order is the thing under test. Mechanics evidence only, never balance.

assert.why: all six records left the vault and the stash grew by exactly the sum of the engine prices the reply, the records and the stash read-back agree on
six sold lines in the journal
the order ended done, nothing was queued for a town visit

scenarios.notes: Hero in town, 6 unidentified magic vault records, 7200 stash gold, knob loot.vaultSellInstant 1. The order is posted to /api/vault/sell with confirm and ack. Expected: the records are Sold and gone from the live vault, the stash rose by exactly the sale gold the reply states (the sum of `item price` of each record's bytes at the default vendor), no item was created in the hero. RED on today's main: Sell only queues for the next town visit. Records are unidentified, so each is priced as its base (the engine pays no affix value for an unidentified item).
